claim: For all coprime integers \(p,q>1\) and every integer \(s>1\) with \(\gcd(s,pq)=1\), the torus-knot group \(G_{p,q}=\langle a,b\mid a^p=b^q\rangle\) embeds in \(G_{pq,s}=\langle x,y\mid x^{pq}=y^s\rangle\) via \(a\mapsto x^q\) and \(b\mapsto yx^p y^{-1}\); the groups are nonisomorphic because their quotients by their infinite cyclic centers are \(C_p*C_q\) and \(C_{pq}*C_s\), respectively.

correctness.rationale: The defining relation is preserved. The quotient map is injective by reduced-word normal form, and the kernel is forced into the central cyclic subgroup, whose generator maps to an infinite-order element.

evidence: Myers, arXiv:math/9901106, Lemma 4.1 states the if-and-only-if only for prime \(p,q,r,s\).
The new formula allows arbitrary coprime \(p,q>1\) and composite target exponent \(pq\), with \(\gcd(s,pq)=1\).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The source theorem does not cover this parameter regime. The quotient map works because \(C_p\) and \(C_q\) embed as distinct conjugate subgroups of the same \(C_{pq}\) factor, a configuration excluded by the prime-target case when the target factors are distinct primes.

The new proof explicitly constructs \(\phi(a)=x^q\) and \(\phi(b)=yx^p y^{-1}\), then proves injectivity via the quotient and central kernel.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prime-only lemma neither asserts nor implies that the same parameter-rigidity conclusion holds for composite target exponents. The new family is an explicit counterexample to that natural extension. The general subgroup-classification literature was not exhaustively searched, so the conclusion is restricted to the exact proved family.

originality.rationale: Myers, arXiv:math/9901106, Section 4, Lemma 4.1 treats only prime parameters. The explicit composite-exponent family is not stated there; it uses two distinct conjugates of cyclic subgroups in \(C_{pq}\). The claim is deliberately limited to this construction, not a classification.
residual_risks: A complete survey of all subgroup-embedding classifications for torus-knot groups was not performed.
The result is a sufficient family only; other embeddings may exist outside the stated divisibility pattern.
